Why is Python called Python? The name comes from the British comedy group Monty Python, not the snake. And Monty Python is a British surreal comedy group that created the sketch comedy television show Monty Python's Flying Circus, which first aired on the BBC about 50 years ago. The creator of Python, Guido van Rossum, was a big fan of Monty Python's Flying Circus. And also he believed that a name that was short, unique, and slightly mysterious would be a good name for a programming language. Also, he thought that programming language should be not only convenient to use and easy to learn, but also fun to work with.

Python Language IS

  • easy to start using
  • free and open source
  • (almost) portable
  • high-level
  • interpreted, not compiled
  • well suited for REPL = Read Eval Print Loop

Everything in Python is an object

Every object has:

  • id — where it's located (~memory address)
  • type — a set of values and operations on these values
  • value — the actual value

Size of INT in Python language

What do you think, how much memory INT takes?

  • In general, 1 bit represents only two values (it's 0 or 1)
  • 1 byte = 8 bits, and this already represents integers from 0 to 255 or from -127 to 127

Can it be depending on the platform:

  • 4 bytes (32 bits) or
  • 8 bytes (64 bits)?

Why so much and not the same?

Cpython open source realization: 


									struct _longobject {
										// macros with
										// 1. the object’s reference counter (8 bytes)
										// 2. and a pointer to the corresponding type object (8 bytes)
										// 3. and extension field ob_size (8 bytes)
										PyObject_VAR_HEAD
										// int value adds 0, 4 (32x) or 8 bytes (64x)
										// SUM(for i=0 through abs(ob_size)-1) ob_digit[i] * 2**(SHIFT*i)
										digit ob_digit[1];
									};
